name: Berlioz Dreamy
description:
Berlioz is our heirloom-tier kids bed — built to the same construction standard as our adult upholstered range, dimensioned for a child today, designed to look correct in the room a teenager will inhabit a decade from now. It's the piece for the parents who'd rather buy once and hand it down.

The thinking: most kids beds sold in India are a category problem. They're either novelty pieces (the race-car bed, the princess bed) that look out of place by the time the child is ten, or they're flimsy budget builds that don't survive a single move. Neither makes sense if you think about a child's bed across a fifteen-year horizon. Berlioz is built on a different premise: a fully upholstered headboard, an adult-grade frame, and a design language that reads as quietly elegant rather than themed — so the bed doesn't need replacing when the room outgrows the theme.

Construction: 18mm BWP plywood frame, the same thickness we use across our adult bed range. Reinforced corner blocks at every load point. The headboard is fully upholstered with 32-density foam padding over a structured backing — the kind of headboard a child can sit up against to read without the cushion compressing flat. Slat support across the mattress base, sized for a standard single or queen mattress depending on configuration. No exposed hardware at any contact point; rounded edges on every approach surface.

Materials: full 4,000-fabric library, with a curated kids-friendly subset highlighted in the configurator — performance fabrics that handle spills, easy-clean velvets, and washable linen blends. The performance fabric tier is what we'd recommend for younger children (washes well, doesn't pill, stands up to glitter and crayon). Solid wood legs in a choice of finishes. Non-toxic finishes throughout.

Configuration: single (standard kids size), single XL (longer for taller children), or queen (for the parents who prefer the bed to be the room's permanent fixture). Specify headboard height — standard or tall. Specify fabric and color from the configurator. The bed converts cleanly between configurations as the child grows; we'll re-upholster the headboard at cost if the room aesthetic changes in five years.

Lead time 14–25 days. Seven-year structural frame warranty, three-year foam and cushion core warranty (two years for Super Soft foam), and one-year upholstery workmanship warranty. Lifetime re-upholstery at cost — meaning the same bed can carry a child from age four through to college, with a fresh fabric refresh whenever the room mood shifts.

name: Camfo
description:
Camfo is the bed for bedrooms with a limited visual budget. Square headboard, clean lines, no tufting, no flutes, no scrolls — a single piece of considered upholstery without ornament. The kind of bed that lets a wall colour, a piece of art, or a curtain do the talking.

The simplicity is the engineering. Square upholstery is harder to do well than tufted upholstery — there's nothing for the eye to land on, so every imperfection in the seam is visible. Our team uses single-needle topstitch at eight stitches per inch on the visible edges, which is denser than the standard for this price tier. The corners are mitered by hand, not machine-folded.

name: Ethiya
description:
Ethiya is the bed for bedrooms designed in the last five years. The headboard is taller than Camfo's but cleaner than Cazewell's — a structured panel with subtle vertical channel-stitching that catches light without dominating it. The proportion is sized for ceilings between 9 and 11 feet.

The channel-stitching is mechanical-but-careful. Each line of stitching runs from headboard top to bottom in a single pass, no joins, with the foam underneath compressed to maintain an even depth. It looks simple. It is not.

We see Ethiya often in second-home purchases — customers who already have an estré sofa or a Cazewell bed, and want a bedroom that's a step ahead of where they started.

name: Matita
description:
Matita is the bed for bedrooms that lean modern but reject cold. The headboard is broad and low, padded with the same foam grade as our sofas, sized for proper sit-up reading without needing extra pillows. Not the tallest headboard in our range — Cazewell wins that — but the most comfortable to actually use.

The construction details matter on this piece. Heavier 18mm plywood frame than our entry beds; reinforced corners; mortise-and-tenon joinery on load-bearing joints. The hydraulic lift platform is rated for 50,000 cycles, which translates to roughly 30 years of daily lift-and-store at typical residential use. The hydraulics are soft-close — no slam when the platform drops, even with bedding piled on it.

Matita is the premium tier of our bedroom range. The customers who buy Matita usually keep their previous bed for the guest room — they don't replace it.

name: Tempah
description:
Tempah is built differently. Where most of our beds use plywood and Indonesian pine, Tempah uses Neem wood and 18mm plywood — heavier, more thermally stable, less prone to swelling in monsoon. It's the bed for homes that aren't air-conditioned year-round, where wood-stable construction quietly matters.

The joinery is mortise-and-tenon on every load-bearing joint — no nails, no screws on the frame elements that carry weight. The frame is held together by the wood itself. This is slower to build and more expensive to source than the standard pine-and-screw construction, but it's also the joinery that lets a bed last 20 years instead of 8.

The diwan-cot variant works as a guest-room or daybed piece — the same Tempah frame in a flat-platform configuration that doubles as a couch when not slept in.
